title: Projective morphisms and projective schemes
statement: A morphism of schemes $f:X\to Y$ [def-pc-scheme] is *projective* in the convention of this blueprint if there are an integer $N\geq0$ and a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_Y$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] such that $f=\pi\circ i$, where $\pi:\mathbf P^N_Y\to Y$ is the structural projection. Here $\mathbf P^N_Y=\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,N\};Y)$ is the projective space over $Y$ with $N+1$ homogeneous coordinates and its structural morphism, as defined in [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. This is the H-projective (finite projective-space embedding) convention. For a field $k$ [def-weil-field], a scheme $X$ over $k$ has a specified structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; it is *projective over $k$* if that structure morphism is projective in the convention just defined.

mathlib_searches.query: Projective morphism of schemes defined by closed immersion into projective space over the base
A morphism of schemes is projective if it factors as a closed immersion into finite dimensional projective space over the base followed by projection
